root.label: Lambdas and Closure Types
root.note: Every lambda expression lowers to a unique unnamed closure struct holding captured members and operator().

children.label: Closure Type Anatomy
children.note: The compiler synthesizes an unnamed non-union class type for each lambda expression.

children.label: Unique unnamed struct
children.note: Two identical lambda expressions still produce two distinct closure types.

children.label: const-by-default operator()
children.note: By-value captures are read-only inside operator() unless mutable removes const.

children.label: Implicitly constexpr calls
children.note: A lambda's operator() is implicitly constexpr whenever its body satisfies constant-expression rules.

children.label: Capture Modes
children.note: Capture clauses define which local variables become value or reference members in the closure.

children.label: Value captures and mutable
children.note: Value captures copy variables at lambda creation; mutable permits mutating the closure's copies.

children.label: Reference captures bind aliases
children.note: Reference captures store aliases to outer variables and can mutate them without mutable.

children.label: Init-capture moves ownership
children.note: C++14 init-captures deduce member types so move-only handles transfer into the closure.

children.label: Non-odr constexpr reads
children.note: Reading a local constexpr value without taking its address needs no capture.

children.label: Object and Lifetime Traps
children.note: Dangling reference captures and implicit this pointer captures are common lifetime hazards.

children.label: Dangling reference captures
children.note: Closures outliving local variables with reference captures cause undefined behavior when invoked.

children.label: [=, this] captures pointer
children.note: C++20 deprecated bare [=] capturing this silently; [=, this] makes pointer capture explicit.

children.label: [=, *this] copies object
children.note: C++17 [*this] stores a full copy of the enclosing object inside the closure.

children.label: Stateless and Unevaluated
children.note: Captureless lambdas behave as zero-overhead stateless callables and function-pointer sources.

children.label: Converts to function pointer
children.note: Captureless lambdas expose a constexpr conversion to a matching C function pointer.

children.label: Default constructible in C++20
children.note: Captureless closure types can be default-constructed and copy-assigned as comparator types.

children.label: Allowed in decltype types
children.note: C++20 allows lambdas in unevaluated operands such as unique_ptr custom deleters.

children.label: Generic and C++23 Extensions
children.note: Modern revisions turned lambdas into full template and recursive callable primitives.

children.label: auto parameters create templates
children.note: Each auto parameter generates an independent template type parameter on operator().

children.label: Explicit template parameter list
children.note: C++20 <class T> syntax exposes deduced types directly for constraints and forwarding.

children.label: this auto self recursion
children.note: C++23 explicit object parameters enable self-recursion, while static operator() drops unused this.
